DESCRIPTION: Primary fraud signal. Fraud-tier claims average
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This field captures the actual reimbursement disbursed to the billing provider or supplier after claim adjudication. In fraud analytics it is the single most important monetary measure because abnormally large values, especially when clustered within a narrow date window or concentrated among a small set of providers, are the clearest indicator of improper or inflated billing. It anchors z-score, percentile, and outlier analyses and serves as the primary dollar axis in scatter and time-series visualizations.

DESCRIPTION: Total dollar amount paid to the provider or supplier for the claim; the primary indicator of payment exposure and the main fraud signal
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This field captures the actual reimbursement disbursed to the billing provider or supplier after claim adjudication. In fraud analytics it is the single most important monetary measure because abnormally large values, especially when clustered within a narrow date window or concentrated among a small set of providers, are the clearest indicator of improper or inflated billing. It anchors z-score, percentile, and outlier analyses and serves as the primary dollar axis in scatter and time-series visualizations.

DESCRIPTION: Natural-log transform of the amount paid to the provider, used to normalize skewed payment values for statistical and correlation analysis
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This is the natural-logarithm transformation of the amount paid to the provider, computed as the log of the value plus a small constant to handle zeros. Because raw payment amounts are heavily right-skewed, the log version compresses extreme high-dollar outliers so that both normal claims and fraudulent spikes remain visible within the same chart. It is the preferred form for correlation matrices, clustering, and any model that assumes a roughly symmetric feature distribution.

DESCRIPTION: Interest dollars paid to the provider due to late claim processing; elevated values can indicate billing-timing manipulation
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This field records interest dollars paid to the provider as a result of claims that were not processed within the statutory payment window. While ordinarily small and benign, unusually high interest amounts can reveal deliberate billing-timing manipulation, resubmission patterns, or attempts to exploit payment-floor rules, making it a useful secondary fraud signal when evaluated alongside the principal paid amount.

DESCRIPTION: Natural-log transform of the provider interest amount, used to normalize the distribution for modeling and visualization
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This is the natural-logarithm transformation of the provider interest amount. It normalizes a sparse, right-skewed monetary field so that the relatively rare large interest payments do not dominate distance-based or correlation calculations, allowing the variable to contribute meaningfully to clustering and anomaly-detection models.

DESCRIPTION: Deductible dollar amount applied to the claim; near-zero values may signal improper deductible waiver
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This field reflects the deductible dollar amount applied to the claim and paid by or on behalf of the beneficiary. In legitimate billing it clusters around the annual Part B deductible, but values at or near zero across many claims for a single provider may indicate systematic deductible waiver, an illegal inducement that removes the beneficiary's financial stake in the service rendered.

DESCRIPTION: Natural-log transform of the deductible paid, used to normalize the distribution for analysis
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This is the natural-logarithm transformation of the deductible paid. The transformation stabilizes the variance of a field that is otherwise bounded and clustered, supporting distribution comparisons and the detection of providers whose deductible patterns deviate sharply from the norm.

DESCRIPTION: Dollar amount offset against the provider for prior identified overpayments; non-zero values flag providers already under recoupment
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This field captures dollars withheld or offset against the provider to recover prior identified overpayments. Any non-zero value is significant because it shows the provider was already under active recoupment; continued and escalating billing by such a provider is a strong recidivism signal and a hallmark of bust-out fraud schemes.

DESCRIPTION: Natural-log transform of the provider offset amount, used to normalize skewed values for analysis
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This is the natural-logarithm transformation of the provider offset amount. Because most claims carry no offset, the log form floors the many zero values while still differentiating the magnitude of active recoupments, letting the variable function as a graded recidivism indicator in models and visualizations.

DESCRIPTION: Coinsurance dollar amount owed on the claim; values far below the standard twenty percent may indicate improper coinsurance waiver
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This field records the coinsurance dollar amount owed on the claim, normally twenty percent of the allowed amount. Values substantially below that benchmark, particularly near zero, suggest improper coinsurance waiver, which like deductible waiver constitutes an unlawful inducement and is a recurring feature of fraudulent DME billing.

DESCRIPTION: Natural-log transform of the coinsurance amount, used to normalize the distribution for correlation analysis
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This is the natural-logarithm transformation of the coinsurance amount. It normalizes the field for inclusion in correlation matrices, where the breakdown of the expected proportional relationship between coinsurance and the paid amount becomes a detectable fraud signature.

DESCRIPTION: Medicare-approved allowed dollar amount for the claim, serving as the benchmark for evaluating submitted and paid amounts
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This field represents the Medicare-approved allowed amount for the claim, the ceiling against which submitted charges and actual payments are evaluated. It provides the reference point for identifying upcoding and overbilling, since a wide and persistent gap between allowed and submitted amounts is a documented fraud pattern.

DESCRIPTION: Natural-log transform of the allowed amount, used to normalize skewed values for analysis
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This is the natural-logarithm transformation of the allowed amount. By compressing the skewed dollar distribution it keeps the variable comparable in scale to other log-transformed monetary features, improving the behavior of clustering algorithms and correlation analysis.

DESCRIPTION: Cumulative Medicare dollars paid to the provider across claims; used to identify providers with abnormally high total payments
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This field aggregates the cumulative Medicare dollars paid to a provider across all of their claims. It elevates the analysis from the individual claim to the provider level, exposing suppliers whose total program payments are abnormally high relative to peers and serving as a core dimension for provider-level fraud segmentation.

DESCRIPTION: Natural-log transform of total Medicare payments, commonly used as the X-axis in fraud scatter analysis
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This is the natural-logarithm transformation of total Medicare payments. It is the conventional X-axis for fraud scatter plots because it allows providers spanning several orders of magnitude in total payments to be displayed and compared on a single, interpretable scale.

DESCRIPTION: Average Medicare payment per unique beneficiary served; an unusually high ratio is a strong utilization-based fraud signal
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This field expresses the average Medicare payment per unique beneficiary served by a provider, combining cost and volume into one utilization ratio. An unusually high value indicates that a provider is extracting large dollars from a small patient base, one of the strongest single indicators of utilization-driven fraud such as patient recycling or phantom billing.

DESCRIPTION: Natural-log transform of payments per beneficiary, commonly used as the Y-axis in fraud scatter analysis
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This is the natural-logarithm transformation of payments per beneficiary. It is the conventional Y-axis for fraud scatter plots, pairing with log total payments to produce the characteristic separation of high-risk providers into a dense upper-right cluster.

DESCRIPTION: Count of distinct beneficiaries served by the provider; a low count paired with high dollars suggests patient recycling
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This field counts the distinct beneficiaries associated with a provider's claims and serves as the denominator for utilization ratios. A low beneficiary count combined with high total payments is a powerful red flag, pointing to patient brokering, identity reuse, or fabricated encounters.

DESCRIPTION: Identifier of the billing supplier on the claim; used to aggregate claim activity to the supplier level
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This field identifies the supplier that submitted the claim and is the primary key for rolling claim-level activity up to the supplier level. Aggregation on this identifier reveals concentration patterns, where a handful of suppliers account for a disproportionate share of high-dollar or high-risk claims.

DESCRIPTION: Health Insurance Claim Number identifying the beneficiary; used to count distinct beneficiaries and detect patient brokering
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This field is the Health Insurance Claim Number identifying the Medicare beneficiary on the claim. Beyond linking claims to patients, it enables distinct-beneficiary counts per supplier that surface patient brokering schemes, where many high-dollar claims trace back to comparatively few unique beneficiaries.

DESCRIPTION: Category of the claim such as DME, orthotics, oxygen, or supplies; used to segment claims by service type
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This field categorizes the claim by service line such as durable medical equipment, orthotics, oxygen, or supplies. It supports segmentation of billing behavior by service type and helps isolate the categories, predominantly DME in this dataset, where fraudulent activity concentrates.

DESCRIPTION: Primary diagnosis code supporting medical necessity; vague or mismatched codes are a documentation-fraud signal
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This field holds the primary diagnosis code that must justify the medical necessity of the item or service billed. Vague, generic, or clinically mismatched codes relative to the equipment supplied are a leading documentation-fraud signature and a frequent basis for claim denial and investigation.

DESCRIPTION: Date the claim was paid; used for time-series and spike-detection analysis of billing behavior
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This field records the date the claim was paid and is the temporal backbone of the analysis. It drives time-series and spike-detection views that expose coordinated billing surges, such as end-of-cycle bust-out patterns timed immediately before month-end review processes.

DESCRIPTION: Internal unique provider identifier used to join claim records to the provider master table
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This field is the internal unique provider identifier used to join claim records to the provider master table. It guarantees reliable provider-level aggregation even when external identifiers change, and underpins every analysis that combines claim metrics with provider attributes.

DESCRIPTION: National Provider Identifier for the provider or supplier; the standard external identifier in fraud referrals
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This field is the National Provider Identifier, the standardized ten-digit external identifier for the provider or supplier. It is the identifier used in fraud referrals, exclusion checks, and cross-system reconciliation, making it essential for connecting internal findings to enterprise and federal records.

DESCRIPTION: Last name of the provider or supplier; used for display and provider-level identification
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This field carries the last name of the provider or supplier and is used primarily for display, reporting, and analyst-facing identification. In provider-level visualizations it labels the entities driving suspicious billing, translating abstract identifiers into recognizable names.

DESCRIPTION: Flag indicating whether the provider was classified as high fraud risk by the PAL predictive model (TRUE or FALSE)
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This field is a boolean flag indicating whether the provider was classified as high fraud risk by the PAL predictive model prior to claim review. As model output joined to the live claims stream, it converts a static risk score into an operational early-warning signal, allowing flagged providers' billing surges to be intercepted before payment.

DESCRIPTION: Document Control Number uniquely identifying the individual claim record
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This field is the Document Control Number that uniquely identifies each individual claim record. It is the grain of the dataset and the key used for claim-level deduplication, traceability, and linkage back to source systems during investigation.

DESCRIPTION: Ground-truth risk label (High, Medium, or Low) assigned for demonstration and model-validation purposes
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This field is a ground-truth risk label of High, Medium, or Low assigned for demonstration and model-validation purposes. It allows analysts to confirm that detection techniques correctly recover known fraudulent records and should be removed before any blind or production evaluation.
